svg.title: Visual abstract: Benchmarking somatic variant calling in melanoma
svg.desc: Three Nextflow DSL2 pipelines call somatic SNVs, indels, structural variants and copy number on the COLO829 melanoma tumor and matched normal, benchmarked against published truth sets, plus RNA-seq of 120 TCGA-SKCM patients. Manta reached 100 percent SV precision, SNV recall reached 81.5 percent after a genome-build bug in the truth set was fixed, a CDKN2A-spanning loss on 9p was recovered, 3,527 genes differed between metastatic and primary tumors, and TMB correlated with an IFN-gamma signature (rho 0.21).
svg.text: VISUAL ABSTRACT · CANCER GENOMICS · NEXTFLOW DSL2 · COLO829 MELANOMA
Benchmarking somatic variant calling in melanoma
Three Nextflow pipelines (WES, WGS-style, RNA-seq), each scored against published ground truth
COLO829 tumor vs matched normal COLO829BL
COLO829 comes with a published truth set
of somatic SNVs, indels and structural
variants. As a result, every caller here
is scored for precision and recall
Only chr9 and chr20 are streamed from
the remote ENA BAMs, which keeps the
run on a laptop. In addition, chr9
carries CDKN2A, a key melanoma gene.
Truth sets: Valle-Inclan et al. 2022, SMaHT
The SNV truth set was on GRCh38 and
the calls on GRCh37. Lifting it over
Nextflow DSL2 with conda, Docker or Singularity profiles, run inside WSL2
Structural variants came back with zero false positives, a CDKN2A-spanning deletion emerged from
pipeline output, and fixing a genome-build bug in the truth set raised SNV recall from 5.7% to 81.5%.
